items.stimulus: At Tuskegee Institute in Alabama, agricultural scientist George Washington Carver developed <u>new and innovative uses</u> for peanuts and sweet potatoes. items.stimulus: In the late 1940s, marine biologist Rachel Carson studied tidal pools along Maine’s rocky coast. Her survey documented how changes in water temperature affected organisms living between the tides. Carson’s team visited the same pools at regular intervals, recording species and measuring salinity. At the end of the first season, the researchers compiled their observations into <u>a catalog</u> of more than 200 organisms. The catalog showed that several species appeared only during brief periods of unusually warm water.
items.explanation: Each correctly indicates that the researchers numbered specimens one at a time. Every is unnecessary because each already conveys the intended meaning.

items.stem:
At that point in time, museums often lacked specimens from remote areas. Mexia carefully recorded each plant's location and habitat before pressing it for preservation. She sent a total of 250 specimens to the University of California herbarium. Some of her samples grew in close proximity to streams, where moisture supported unusual vegetation.

Her field notes helped later researchers compare plants from distant regions. Because of this, Mexia's work contributed to a clearer understanding of Mexico's flora.

items.stimulus: During the summer of 1935, botanist Ynes Mexia <u>began to start collecting</u> plants in Mexico. Her goal was to document species from regions that had received little scientific attention. In the year 1936, she traveled through the state of Oaxaca with local guides. Mexia returned back to Berkeley with hundreds of specimens, many of which had never been described by scientists. The reason why her collection mattered was its geographic breadth.
items.explanation: The verb began already expresses the start of an action, so "began collecting" is concise and grammatical. "Began to start" repeats the same idea.

items.stem: Which is the best version of the underlined portion?
items.stimulus: During the summer of 1935, botanist Ynes Mexia began to start collecting plants in Mexico. Her goal was to document species from regions that had received little scientific attention. In the year 1936, she traveled through the state of Oaxaca with local guides. Mexia returned back to Berkeley with hundreds of specimens, many of which had never been described by scientists. The reason why her collection mattered was its geographic breadth. At that point in time, museums often lacked specimens from remote areas. Mexia carefully recorded each plant's location and habitat before pressing it for preservation. She sent <u>a total of 250 specimens</u> to the University of California herbarium. Some of her samples grew in close proximity to streams, where moisture supported unusual vegetation. Her field notes helped later researchers compare plants from distant regions. Because of this, Mexia's work contributed to a clearer understanding of Mexico's flora.
items.explanation: "250 specimens" states the quantity directly. Both "a total of" and "in total" repeat information already conveyed by the number, and "a total number of" is even more cumbersome.

per_choice.correct: "250 specimens" states the quantity directly. Both "a total of" and "in total" repeat information already conveyed by the number, and "a total number of" is even more cumbersome.
per_choice.trap: Phrases such as "a total of" can seem useful when reporting numbers, but the number itself already communicates the complete quantity here.
